svg.title: Wire bond design rules: generic values and where each comes from
svg.text: Generic starting values for a die bonded to a board, each labelled by where it comes from. Nobody on this team has bonded yet, so every value is also a question for the bonding house.
5 rules. Read in a published standard (MIL-STD-883).
17 rules. Read in a packaging house, vendor or bonding lab guide.
1 rule. Read as a rule of thumb in a published source.
5 rules. Ours. No source found: change it before trusting it.

svg.text: In the app: every wire, including wires left to the bonder; sized wires, only wires of a type with a diameter or loop, the rest counted as not checked; not yet, shown in the DRC rules panel as not enforced, never as a pass.
A tripped placeholder only ever warns. Values for 25 µm wire scale with diameter where the source gives a table: see the condition and the sources file, docs/wire_bond_design_rules_sources.md.
What does “too long” mean? Our best answer so far
There is no one number. A wire is too long when the first of these four limits bites, and
which one bites depends on the wire, the process and the signal.
The bonding house's maximum for that wire. Europractice: 6 mm for 25 µm Au
ball (4.5, 5.0, 6.0, 7.0 mm for 17.5 to 33 µm). Samtec: 6.35 mm. This is W1,
Sag and sweep grow with span over diameter. The 100-D rule caps span at 100
wire diameters, 2.5 mm for 25 µm wire. It comes from molded packages, where
mold flow pushes wires; a glob top flows too. This is W2.
A long, low wire sags towards the die edge and its neighbours. MIL-STD-883
rejects less than 2 wire diameters to a bare die edge or another wire (class
S). These are S2 and W6.
1 mil Au wire has about 25 pH and 1.17 mΩ per mil: roughly 1 nH and 46 mΩ per
mm. Too long is when that matters to the signal. No limit is set for this.
What the app does today: W1 measures the straight plan distance from first bond to second, which
is shorter than the wire by its loop, and warns over 6 mm. It runs on every wire, including those
left to the bonder. W2 runs only where a type gives a diameter.
Open questions, and what would answer each
What does too long mean for us?
The house's maximum length per wire diameter and loop height; whether we glob top, since flow sweeps
wires; the edge rates of our fastest signals.
Which wire: Au or Al, what diameter, ball or wedge?
The house's standard wire. It sets P1, P2, P4, W1 and W2, which are quoted here for 25 µm Au ball.
Capillary or wedge tip size and bond head drawings. They set K1, P6, L4 and the pitches.
The encapsulant datasheet and how it is dispensed. It sets S4, S5 and L5.
How tall are the parts near the die?
Heights from the board's parts list. With them the app could enforce K1.
Do we want an inspection class?
MIL-STD-883 class S, class B, or commercial. It sets W6, S2 and B1 to B3.
How thick is the die, and how thick the attach?
Measured or from the foundry. L3 takes twice the thickness; S1 and D2 depend on it.
Are lands 150 µm from the die acceptable?
Our example board has them; Samtec asks 375 µm without a ground plane. Ask the house about die
What step does a stacked die need?
No source found. D2 is a placeholder borrowed from die to die spacing.
MIL-STD-883G, TM 2010.11 internal visual (monolithic) and TM 2017.8 (hybrid), 2004. Bond size, separation, crossings.
Europractice, ASIC prototype packaging design rules, 2024. Pad, pitch, length, angle, wires per pad, die to die.
Samtec, precision die attach design rules and guidelines, 2017. Land size and pitch, die edge to land, loop height, encapsulation.
STFC Interconnect Laboratory, helpful guidelines (G. Lockwood). 45° head clearance, 3 × d ball pads, 100 × 125 µm wedge pads.
CERN bond lab, recommendations. 60 µm pitch with 25 µm wire; 300 µm between two in-line bonds.
US patent 5,923,092. The 100-D rule for maximum span; 180 to 200 mil in industry at the time.
Semiconductor Digest, Wire bonding considerations. 25 pH and 1.17 mΩ per mil of 1 mil Au wire.
Read and not used as a default: an LCSC blog (≤ 5 mm length, 60 to 120 µm ball pads), an Altium article (50 to 150 µm lands). Full notes and quotes: docs/wire_bond_design_rules_sources.md.
Generated from the rule table in app/js/rules.js by app/make_rules_svg.py. The app's DRC rules panel uses the same table, and a test checks they agree.
